item.title: Risk of flooding still a possibility despite rain clearing
item.description: The risk of flooding hasn't gone away, despite rain clearing. The National Emergency Co-ordination Group is due to meet again today, as it continues to monitor river levels after almost two weeks of heavy rain. The group says surface flooding is still a problem in some parts of the country. item.title: Gardaí appeal for information on damaged machinery at local ESB site
item.description: Gardai are appealing for information after machinery was damaged and diesel was stolen at an ESB site in Cootehill. According to Gardai, between the hours of 3pm on the 26th of January and 8am on the 28th of January, staff returned to an ESB site in Mountain Lodge, Cootehill and found a piece of machinery damaged. item.title: Local TD does not want to see complete ban on e-scooters
item.description: A local TD has said that he does not want to see a complete ban on e-scooters. Fine Gael TD, David Maxwell highlighted that a lot of people use the scooters to get to work. It comes following a ban on scrambler bikes implemented by the government this week. Deputy Maxwell believes that e-scooters should be kept on the road or on cyclepaths. Speaking to Northern Sound, he said that e-scooters need to be kept off footpaths. Advertisement

item.title: More than 370 retention permission applications submitted locally
item.description: More than 370 applications for retention permission have been submitted in the last two years. An investigation by the Irish Independent on the "build first, ask for permission later" culture revealed more than half of all retention applications lodged since January 2024 have been approved by local authorities across the country. item.title: Local councillor calls on Telecom Éireann to address fallen poles along roads
item.description: A local councillor has called on Telecom Éireann to address the issue of fallen and overhanging poles along roads. Cllr Winston Bennet made the calls when he brought a motion to the monthly meeting of Ballyjamesduff Municipal District on the issue. The Fine Gael councillor says there is a major safety issue in relation to overhanging poles and they pose a risk to motorists. item.title: Longford get the better of Monaghan
item.description: Monaghan fell to Longford in their Allianz hurling league division four meeting played at Cloghan. Joe Rabbit, Martin Farrell and Reuben Murray points helped the farney into a six point lead after 23 minutes, Longford lading eight points to two. Monaghan were reduced to 14 players on the stroke of half-time when James Brady was shown a red card. Longford took a nine point lead to the break, 12 points to three.
